verdict.line: You lose if Mordekaiser pulls you into an extended trade; you win if you burst off auto-shields and reset before his passive stacks.

brief.thesis: Camille wants short, decisive exchanges off her passive shield and Q burst, but Mordekaiser's kit is built to punish exactly that: his E (Death's Grasp) drags her into range, and three landed hits flip on his passive Darkness Rise aura while his W (Indestructible) banks damage into a heal. The head-to-head (49.9% over 1941 games) and the lane/solo-kill edge both sitting with Mordekaiser confirm this is a lane you win by dictating tempo, not by slugging it out.

theirWindow.what: Once you're pulled into his range he'll chain Q (Obliterate) and bank damage into W (Indestructible); disengage immediately rather than trading through it, since every extra hit he lands builds toward his 3-hit passive aura.

yourWindow.when: Right after your auto lands (shield up)
yourWindow.what: Adaptive Defenses just gave you a magic-damage shield — this is the window OP.GG flags to trade one-sidedly. Fire Q (Precision Protocol) and commit the trade now, then reset instead of staying in extended melee.

start.why: Measured at 50.5% over 1571 games (68% pick) — the sustain and auto-attack damage support the short-trade, auto-then-reset pattern this lane demands.

boots.why: 50.9% over 1318 games (66.7% pick); the magic resist directly offsets Mordekaiser's magic damage and his Darkness Rise aura ticks.

core.why: First item in the highest-winrate path (53.2% over 333 games); the burst and move speed are what let you win the Q-then-reset trade instead of getting dragged into his sustain window.
Second item on the same 53.2% path; adds sustained damage and healing to close out skirmishes once his passive stacking becomes a real threat.
Caps the 30.6%-picked core path; damage-over-time mitigation blunts his Obliterate (Q) poke and keeps you alive through his W-fueled sustain.

you need more sustained ability-haste damage against a tankier build
you're getting bursted down in skirmishes and need a health buffer

runes.keystoneWhy: This page measures 51.1% (24.5% pick), the higher of the two recorded pages — the sustained health from proccing Grasp on trades directly counters a lane where you're expected to be on the back foot.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is both the most-picked combo (67.7%) and the highest-winrate (49.1%) in this matchup; Ignite punishes his W-fueled healing on any trade you win. Flash+Teleport (48.5%, 17.5% pick) is the next-best swap if you'd rather prioritize safety and wave management in a lane you're expected to lose tempo in.

playing.title: Track his E before you engage
playing.detail: Death's Grasp is on a 16/14/12/10/8s cooldown and pulls everything in its area — if it's up, don't walk into its 700 range, since getting pulled hands him the extended fight he wants.

playing.title: Trade on autos, not marathons
playing.detail: Use the Adaptive Defenses shield right after an auto lands to fire Q (Precision Protocol) and commit, then disengage instead of staying in prolonged melee where his W sustain and passive aura take over.

playing.title: Pre-plan Hookshot around walls
playing.detail: E (Hookshot, 800 range) only works off a wall — know where your engage/escape walls are before you commit a trade, since you can't reset range without one.

playing.title: Save the Q recast for isolated hits
playing.detail: Precision Protocol's delayed recast does significantly more damage, but only use it when you can safely wait out the window — not as a reflex poke into his 675-range Obliterate.

playing.title: Disengage once his passive is lit
playing.detail: Darkness Rise needs three landed hits to turn on; if he's stacked it mid-trade, back off instead of continuing, since the damage math flips in his favor.

playing.title: Rush Trinity Force every game
playing.detail: It's the first item on the highest-winrate build path (53.2%) and the spike that finally lets you win trades outright around levels 11-15.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning (trade timing, passive stacking, engage patterns) is this brief's own tactical read, not sourced data.
